transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2028-06-21
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Patel, Amira Gomez, Jordan Wu (Redwood); Alex Rivers, Priya Nair, Marco Diaz, Sana Kobayashi (Cyclone AI)
---
Auto-generated Summary:
- Walkthrough of Redwood Console per-route dashboards and cost attribution flows.
- Showed Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization) and how they map to unit cost.
- Discussed tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated and VPC/private deployment needs.
- Agreed next steps: share pricing worksheet, run benchmarks, supply traffic sample.
---
Topics: per-route cost, token accounting, KV cache hits, batching, pilot scope, compliance docs (SOC2/KMS), canary rollouts
Action items (auto): see action_items metadata above

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Liam Patel: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining, um — Alex, Priya, Marco — good to have you. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Alex Rivers: Hey Liam, hey team. Alex here.
[00:08] Priya Nair: Priya — hi.
[00:09] Marco Diaz: Marco — FinOps.
[00:10] Sana Kobayashi: Sana here.
[00:12] Amira Gomez: Amira from Redwood, SE. We'll focus on the console and a couple of Optimize knobs.
[00:17] Jordan Wu: Jordan, product — short note on rollout controls.
[00:19] Liam: Cool. Objective: show how per-route dashboards help you tie spend to product teams and decide whether a route should be served by hosted or dedicated capacity. Also show quick wins where Optimize can cut unit cost without perceptible latency change.
[00:32] Alex: That's the bit we care about — our PM org wants cost per feature, not just token spend.
[00:37] Amira: Yep. I'll share my screen — switching to Console — bear with me, the recording may show a notification.
[00:45] [screen share sound]
[00:48] Amira: So here's the usage overview. Top panel is traffic by route. You can see Route A (chat-assistant) is 42% of tokens, Route B (summarization) 18%, and a bunch of small routes. We tag routes via SDK metadata; you can map those to product slugs.
[01:05] Priya: How do tags get propagated? We currently set a header 'x-cyclone-route' on requests.
[01:08] Amira: Perfect — that flows right into the Console routing table. If you can't change headers, we also support token-level route attribution via SDK mapping.
[01:20] Marco: On the cost side — is console showing gross cost or net after committed credits?
[01:25] Jordan: The dashboard shows raw compute token cost and then overlays committed discounts in the billing tab. So you can see both the per-route raw spend and the amortized charge after discounts.
[01:35] Alex: OK — show me an example where we would reduce cost without hurting latency.
[01:39] Amira: Sure — go to 'Optimize' view. First recommendation is batching: for Route A we see a median latency of 160 ms but 95th of 420 ms. By grouping low-context requests with a 50 ms queueing window we get 20–30% token cost reduction on that route and P95 stays acceptable.
[01:56] Priya: 50 ms queueing? Our SLAs are tight — need to ensure p95 under 500 ms for the assistant route.
[02:02] Amira: Right — in Optimize you'd create a profile: batch window = 50ms, max batch size = 32, route-level override. The console's simulation tool shows expected p95 impact.
[02:12] [small cross-talk]
[02:15] Marco: How reliable are the simulations? We don't want surprises in production.
[02:18] Amira: Simulations use your historical latencies + model perf profiles; they're an estimate — we always recommend gated rollout: canary at 5% then 25% then 100% with auto-fallback.
[02:28] Alex: What about KV cache? We have a lot of repeated prefixes for the assistant.
[02:31] Amira: Good point. Console has a KV cache heatmap per route. For Route A we've observed a 28% cache hit rate — enabling prefix caching plus a slightly higher cache size gives another 12% token drop in our model. Note — sometimes transcription says K V cash — sorry the auto-transcript is weird.
[02:47] Priya: (laughs) Yeah I saw that in the notes.
[02:49] Liam: On infra choices — you mentioned hosted vs dedicated. For Cyclone, any thoughts on which route to pin to Dedicated?
[02:56] Jordan: We typically recommend pinning high-volume, latency-sensitive routes (like user-facing assistant) to Dedicated. Less sensitive batch/scheduled routes can live on Hosted where cost per token is lower at low utilization. The Console route map helps you pick candidates by showing traffic share and cost per token.
[03:12] Sana: If we go Dedicated, how isolated is the data plane? We have customers in EU with residency reqs.
[03:18] Amira: Dedicated pools are tenant-isolated and you can run them in a specific region; for strict residency we offer Private (VPC/on-prem) with a customer-managed control plane. We integrate KMS for key management and produce audit logs for every inference call.
[03:30] Marco: KMS integration — is it BYOK?
[03:33] Amira: Yes, BYOK via your cloud KMS or HSM; we have an onboarding doc. I'll attach the security pack after the meeting.
[03:39] Alex: Can you show the per-token breakdown? We want to understand cost drivers: model compute vs GPU amortization vs network.
[03:45] Amira: On the right panel you have token-level cost slices. Model compute dominates for large generation requests — you'll see token compute, memory, and infra amortization. We also show a per-request breakdown: prompt tokens vs completion tokens vs KV cache savings.
[03:58] Priya: How precise is prompt/completion split? Our internal tokenization is slightly different — we use SentencePiece variant.
[04:04] Amira: Our token counter tries to match the model tokenizer; you can upload a tokenizer map if you have a custom tokenizer and the console will re-hydrate numbers. That will make per-route metrics line up.
[04:14] [pause]
[04:17] Marco: What about currency and exchange rate handling for multi-region billing?
[04:21] Jordan: Billing shows USD natively; the reporting tab can convert to other currencies using daily FX rates for historical comparisons. For invoicing we can set currency per billing profile.
[04:31] Alex: Security and compliance notes — do you have SOC2 and penetration test reports?
[04:35] Amira: Yes — SOC2, ISO summaries, and pen test summaries. Liam will share links post-call.
[04:41] Liam: I'll drop the pack and a short pilot agreement.
[04:44] [07:10 — jump in transcript, slightly misaligned timestamps due to auto-transcript segmentation]
[07:10] Priya: For pilot scope — we want to measure cost delta across 3 routes (Assistant, Summarize, Search). Can Redwood run a 48-hour throughput test and a 2-day canary on our prod mirror?
[07:22] Amira: Yes — we can do a short load test using your artifact. Best practice: shared test dataset, run at scaled QPS to replicate p95 percentiles. We prefer a staging mirror but can run on dedicated isolated capacity for pilot.
[07:36] Alex: Metrics we'll need: per-route token cost, p50/p95 latency, KV cache hit rate, and inference error rate.
[07:43] Amira: We'll export a pilot dashboard and a CSV for your FinOps team.
[07:47] Marco: Any gotchas on billing for a pilot? Fixed minimal charge?
[07:51] Liam: Pilots often run as usage with a capped credit; for Dedicated we can set a short-term reserved pool if you want deterministic performance. We'll include options in the worksheet.
[07:59] Priya: Who will be the single point of contact?
[08:02] Alex: I'll coordinate with Priya and Marco.
[08:05] Liam: Great. Quick demo: I'm going to open a route detail for Assistant — note the timeline view shows a spike last week when you rolled a new prompt. You can drill into individual requests and see token traces.
[08:20] Amira: Also the 'Cost Attribution' tab lets you create an allocation rule — e.g., split infra amortization across routes by request count or by peak GPU minutes. That helps with cross-team chargebacks.
[08:33] Marco: Can we export per-route invoices for internal chargeback?
[08:36] Jordan: Yes — you can generate per-route invoice lines and map them to accounting codes. We have an API to pull that data into your internal systems.
[08:44] Sana: Slightly off-topic — does console capture model version drift and quality regressions? We want contour alerts if output quality drops.
[08:51] Amira: Yep — Redwood has eval hooks. You can attach a probe set and the console will run metrics on new model rollouts and fire regressions. Optimize ties those alerts to rollbacks.
[08:59] Priya: Do you have an example rule?
[09:01] Amira: Example: if Rouge-L drops by >5% on the probe set after a model swap, auto-fallback to previous version and open a ticket.
[09:09] Alex: OK that's useful.
[09:12] Liam: Quick questions from our side — any hard constraints on compliance or audit windows?
[09:16] Priya: We need 1 year of per-request audit logs for some customers and SSO with SAML.
[09:21] Amira: SAML OK, RBAC is built into the Console; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM and retained to your retention policies in Private deployments.
[09:30] Marco: Is there any latency penalty for sending logs to SIEM synchronously?
[09:34] Jordan: We ship audit logs asynchronously so no impact on inference latency.
[09:38] [minor pause]
[09:40] Alex: Let's talk numbers a bit. If Route A is 42% of tokens and we get a combined 32% reduction through batching + cache + quantization, what's the ballpark unit cost change?
[09:52] Amira: For that profile, our bench shows per-token compute drop of about 28%, and end-to-end unit cost drops about 22% after amortization. We'll put concrete numbers in the worksheet.
[10:05] Priya: Quantization — any quality impact?
[10:08] Amira: We recommend int8 or mixed int8 for many workloads. Optimize recommends model variants and quant profiles per route with expected quality impact and you can A/B test them.
[10:18] Marco: Are you supporting recent open models — we use a slightly modified LLaMA variant.
[10:22] Jordan: We onboard models — if it's architecture-compatible we can serve it. For custom variants we run compatibility tests and pick kernels accordingly.
[10:31] Sana: Any limits on max context? We have some long docs up to 32k tokens.
[10:36] Amira: Console supports monitoring for large context runs and you can set per-route max context enforcement to prevent runaway bills. For 32k you may want dedicated memory-optimized instances.
[10:46] [pause, background noise]
[10:50] Marco: On the pilot, will you provide a sandboxed billing view so we can estimate cost ahead of contract?
[10:55] Liam: Yes — the pilot dashboard includes projected monthly run-rate based on the sample traffic you provide.
[11:00] Alex: Good. Any competitor concerns? We've seen other vendors offering aggressive discounts.
[11:05] Liam: Common competitors (Anthropic, OpenAI, Replicate) — the difference is we expose the knobs and measurables to help you optimize cost over time, not just lower list pricing.
[11:16] Priya: Final Q — data residency for EU customers on Private deployment?
[11:20] Amira: Private supports EU-only control plane and data plane. We can sign data processing addenda and map to your DSR needs.
[11:27] Alex: OK let's wrap with next steps.
[11:30] Liam: Recap: 1) Cyclone to share top-10 routes + 30-day sample by 6/23. 2) Redwood to send pricing worksheet, SOC2 + KMS docs by 6/24. 3) SE to run 48-hour bench and 2-day canary window planning target week of 6/26. 4) Schedule a follow-up to review pilot dashboard (tentatively 6/30).
[11:52] Marco: Makes sense.
[11:53] Priya: Thanks all.
[11:55] Alex: Thanks.
[11:57] Amira: Thanks, bye.
[11:59] Liam: Bye everyone.
